notes:
Context: OchreBridge is a mid-market SaaS vendor providing product analytics and in-app guidance. Started on Redwood Hosted API for quick feature rollout (chat-based help, semantic search, reranker). After 8 weeks of pilot, they want Dedicated for cost predictability and VPC isolation. Key asks: predictable monthly egress/compute commitment, burst capacity (able to absorb spikes from weekly training jobs and product launches), and a ramp schedule that aligns with Q3 feature rollouts.

POC findings (from Riley & internal devs):
- Latency: p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 110-120ms on Hosted (good). Customer confirmed SLA requirement p95 <= 150ms for US users.
- Quality: model variant selection = open-vacanza-7b-q4 (customer prefers down-quantized variant for cost tradeoff); want fallback to larger model for policy-critical flows.
- Cost sensitivity: finance projects 6-9 month ROI; high sensitivity to peak overages during product launches.

Pricing/Packaging negotiation specifics discussed:
- Commit levels under consideration: 100k tokens/day baseline (monthly committed), 300k tokens/day (mid), 1M tokens/day (enterprise), with stepped pricing.
- Burst: request included burst pool equal to 20% of committed monthly throughput free; Redwood proposed 10% included + prepaid burst credits; customer pushing for 25% for first 3 months to smooth ramp.
- Overage: customer requests soft overage with throttled rates after 120% of committed, then hard throttle; Redwood proposes tiered overage at 1.5x base price above committed, escalating to 2.0x beyond 200%.
- Ramp schedule: OchreBridge wants 4-month ramp (25% increments each month) tied to monthly usage reviews and ability to adjust committed level up or down with 30-day notice.
- Term & discounts: looking for 12 month commitment with staged discounts: 5% at baseline, 12% at mid commit, 20% at enterprise commit.

Quotes / stakeholder notes:
- CTO (D. Rivera): "We need predictable unit economics during product launches. If overage model blows up, we can't proceed."
- Head of Infra (L. Gupta): "KMS integration timeline is the gating item for Dedicated in our VPC. Need sample SOW clause for key rotation and audit logs."

Next steps (short):
- AE (Jordan) to deliver revised commercial term sheet with: 4-month ramp schedule, 20% burst inclusion first 3 months, explicit overage tiers, SOW security clauses by 2026-03-11.
- SE (Riley) to provide KMS integration plan + 2-week window for validation in staging.
- Legal & procurement: customer to review SOW; planning procurement approval meeting 2026-03-18.

Blockers: pricing alignment on bursts & overage model; legal review of SOW; KMS/SSO go-live date unknown.

Linked artifacts: see drive deck for pricing slides; security checklist spreadsheet; Fireflies links above for transcripts.
